## Goal

Mostra's plugin can be listed in Claude's plugin directory, which serves Claude Code, Cowork and the Claude apps from one listing, while the organization behind it isn't verified: a folder of the plugin's repository that carries the Skill and the remote MCP server and nothing the directory refuses, built from the same source as the full plugin by every release, with the full plugin, its local server and every other harness's manifests exactly as they are.

## Owned requirements

None: a maintenance or design unit owns no requirement (D152). Its progress report's evidence table has one row per item of its scope, each closed by a check through the real public interface (README §3), and the checks it adds extend their owners' rows.

## Scope

From [WORK_PACKAGES.md](../WORK_PACKAGES.md):

- a second build of the harness plugin in the plugin's repository, `claude-directory/`, from the same definition (`tools/plugins/definition.ts`) and the same Skill: `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` with only the fields Claude Code's reference documents, the listing icon, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` for a local install, `.mcp.json` with only the remote MCP server (`mostra-remote`, the definition's `remoteMcp.url`), its own README, and `skills/mostra/` with `SKILL.md`, every reference and each example artifact as one Markdown file, its files in fenced blocks;
- the Skill's links to the examples rewritten in that copy by one named, tested rewrite, and nothing else in the Skill changed;
- a check holding `claude-directory/` to the Claude plugin directory's rules for a plugin from an organization that isn't verified (file types, no local server, no package-manager files and the rest), run by every release beside the harnesses' checks;
- the plugin's root unchanged: everything outside `claude-directory/` is byte for byte what the release built before.

Design detail for this package:

- A maintenance unit (D152): it owns no requirement. Its scope is the four items above, each closed with its check through the real interface and, for the checks, a seeded violation red on the old code; the checks it adds extend AX-10's row (harness plugins from one source).
- **The finding.** The Claude plugin directory reviews a submission's folder with an automatic policy before any person does, and it refused the plugin's 0.18.0 release at the repository's root for two blocking reasons, both because the organization isn't verified: it accepts **local (stdio) MCP servers** only from verified organizations (`.mcp.json`'s `mostra`, `npx -y @mostra/cli@<version> mcp --embedded`), and **files outside its allowed list** only from them too. The list is Markdown, plain text, JSON, YAML and PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP and ICO images; it also rules out files that start with a shebang, package-manager files, other `.claude-plugin` folders, extra `.mcp.json` files and `.svg` files other than the icon. In 0.18.0 the files outside it were the examples' `.tsx`, `.ts` and `.css`. "MCP servers that Claude Code connects to at a public URL can stay." Its warnings, which don't block: a credential read from the user's machine (the samples that pass `secret("…")` to `fetch`, held since the first submission as `MCP_FORWARDS_CREDENTIAL_ENV`), three fields of `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` it doesn't know, and a pinned `npx` launch with no lockfile; its notes: a local MCP server isn't offered on claude.ai, and the Agent Plugins `plugin.json` at the root is ignored. Re-verify all of it at the start, from the listing's report in the developer portal (Mirza opens it) and the directory's published policy, and record it in VERIFIED_FACTS with the date.
- **One listing, a new submission.** The listing's settings offer Claude Code, Cowork and the Claude apps (web, desktop, mobile), and the remote server is also submitted as an MCP connector at the same URL and paired with the listing, as Claude's directory asks of a plugin whose server its organization runs (M98). A submission's source folder can't change, so the new folder is a new submission; the refused one stays, so that once the organization is verified a new version there lists the full plugin and the folder's listing is delisted (M98); the listing keeps the icon of its first submission, so the new one takes the same icon.
- **The folder,** written by `buildPlugin` into the same tree (so the release's build, check and publish steps carry it with no change to `release.yml`, and one tag pins both): `claude-directory/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` with the definition's name, version, description, author, license, keywords, homepage, repository and privacy policy, and the other fields Claude Code's plugins reference documents (the root's manifest as it is: the directory's report named `documentationUrl`, `supportUrl` and `privacyPolicyUrl` as fields it reads for the listing, "no action needed", M98); the icon; `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` with the plugin at `./`, for `claude plugin marketplace add`; `.mcp.json` with only `mostra-remote` (`{ "type": "http", "url": <remoteMcp.url> }`); a README from `readme.ts` with the local server off, which discloses the remote server, its sign-in and its privacy policy, and says where the full plugin and the CLI are; and `skills/mostra/`. A definition flag turns it on, as the plugin's other features are turned on (`tools/plugins/definition.ts`). Nothing in it starts a program, sets where packages come from or reads an environment variable.
- **The examples as Markdown.** Each example artifact (`skills/mostra/assets/examples/<name>/`, after WP-18 `decision`, `inbox`, `dashboard` and `specimen`) becomes `skills/mostra/assets/examples/<name>.md` in the folder: one line saying it is a complete artifact that passes verify and that each block is a file to write into an artifact's directory at the path its heading gives, then each file under a heading with its path and a fenced block in its language (`index.tsx` first), generated by the build, never written by hand. Every link in the folder's Skill to an example's directory (`assets/examples/<name>/`, `../assets/examples/<name>/`) is rewritten to its Markdown file by one exact, tested rewrite; the check fails on any link in the folder that points at a file the folder lacks, and on any other difference from the repository's Skill.
- **Themed without a stylesheet.** Since WP-18 a page names its theme in its manifest (`kit: { theme: "studio" }`) and builds from the kit's parts (`@mostra/kit/*`, `@/components/ui/*`), which need no install and no stylesheet, so the examples hold only `.tsx` and `.ts` files and the Markdown example is the whole artifact. The check that proves it: each Markdown example split back into files (a block's heading names its path) gives the source example's files byte for byte, and that artifact passes `mostra verify --screenshots always` with screenshots that wear the theme, compared with the source example's.
- **The Skill stays one Skill.** The folder's Skill is the repository's with only the link rewrite and its `compatibility` field (below). Its "Running Mostra" section already covers both ways in: Mostra's tools from a connector when they are in the agent's tool list, and the CLI by `npx` otherwise; neither changes where packages come from. If the directory's validator or a reviewer holds a line of the Skill, the change is agent-facing prose drafted with Mirza (D149, D74), made in the repository's Skill unless it is about the directory alone. **The folder's `compatibility` field names both ways in** (Mirza, on the question this spec carried): a shell that runs `mostra` (or `npx` with Node.js 22.19 or later), or Mostra's tools from a connector, which is the only way in on the Claude apps. The repository's Skill keeps its field as it is. The field is changed by the same tested transform as the link rewrite, and the directory-rules check reads it back.
- **The directory check** (`check.ts`, a rule set of its own run on `claude-directory/` beside the harnesses' checks): every file is UTF-8 Markdown, plain text, JSON or YAML, or a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or ICO image; no file starts with `#!`; no `package.json`, lockfile or `.npmrc`-like file; one `.claude-plugin/` and one `.mcp.json`, at the folder's root; no `.svg` but the icon; `.mcp.json` declares no server with a `command`; the manifest has only documented fields; every link resolves inside the folder. Each rule names its source and the date it was read, as `manifests.ts` does, and each is proven by a seeded violation.
- **The root unchanged.** A test builds the plugin with the folder on and off at the same version and asserts that every path outside `claude-directory/` is the same set with the same bytes; the existing harness check (`node tools/plugins/cli.ts check`) still passes, and `claude plugin install mostra@mostra`, Codex's and Gemini CLI's installs of the root still load exactly one Skill and the local server (`tools/plugins/try-harnesses.sh`).
- **Design it twice and choose** (D123): (a) the folder in the plugin's repository, as above; (b) a second repository the release publishes the same build to. Recommended: (a), one repository, one release, one tag; take (b) only if a harness or an indexer that walks the whole repository treats the folder's second copy of the Skill as a second skill, or the validator refuses a folder below a repository that holds code, and record which.
- **What the session does outside the repository, with Mirza:** before acceptance, push a branch of the plugin's repository holding the release candidate's tree to the developer portal (`claude.ai/directory/manage`) as a new submission from `claude-directory/`, run its validation and stop there ("nothing is submitted until you choose to"); record its findings in VERIFIED_FACTS; the portal's checkboxes ignore an automated browser's clicks, so Mirza sets the surfaces and presses the buttons. After the release that carries the folder, Mirza submits it (surfaces Claude Code, Cowork and Claude apps; it transmits user data, with the privacy policy) and submits the remote server as an MCP connector; the refused submission stays (M98).
- Add MT-07's own decision entry (the folder, its check, the examples as Markdown, (a) or (b)), the directory's rules and the refusal in VERIFIED_FACTS, the plugin's playbook (`docs/agents/check-harness-plugins.md`: the folder, its check, the validation in the portal) and a line in the release notes that the plugin's repository has a folder for Claude's directory.

## Out of scope

- Listing the full plugin, with its local server, in Claude's directory: that needs a verified organization.
- Other directories and marketplaces (OpenAI's, Cursor's, Gemini CLI's and the rest) and their manifests, which are unchanged.
- Changing what the examples do to quiet a warning: a sample that passes a secret to `fetch` stays true to how actions are written, and its warning is for the reviewer.
- The submission itself and the listing's settings, which are Mirza's in the portal.

## Acceptance evidence

one row per scope item, each closed through the real interface: the directory check red on each seeded violation and green on the built folder; the root's snapshot equal to the build without the folder, and the harnesses' check still green; each Markdown example reassembled into an artifact passes `mostra verify --screenshots always` with the theme's look in both screenshots; the folder installed in Claude Code from disk loads the Skill and only the remote server, which signs in and runs the loop through its tools (external); the developer portal's own validator reads a submission of the folder, validated and not submitted, with no blocking finding (external, with Mirza).

Also: `pnpm check` green, diff reviewed, the progress report's evidence table complete for every owned requirement (README §3), the evidence matrix regenerated, docs and AGENTS.md current, and the report finalized after acceptance (README §4).

## Risks and notes

- A second copy of the Skill in one repository can be listed twice by an indexer that walks every `SKILL.md`: check what the harnesses and the public skill indexes do with it, and take (b) if it matters.
- The directory's rules are its own and change: the check names each rule's source and date, and a release that the portal refuses again is a finding for the next unit, not a reason to loosen the check.
- The folder must never drift from the root: it is built from the same definition and Skill in the same run, and the tests compare both to their sources.
- The remote server's URL is the same before and after any change of where the service runs, so the listing needs no new submission when it moves.

## Handoff

Every release publishes a `claude-directory/` in the plugin's repository that Claude's plugin directory accepts from an organization that isn't verified, with the Skill and the remote server, built and checked with the full plugin unchanged. Mirza submits it as a new listing for Claude Code, Cowork and the Claude apps, and the remote server as a connector paired with it; once the organization is verified, a new version of the refused submission lists the full plugin and the folder's listing is delisted.
